{"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "For each firm compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in cost of goods sold (item COGS), using annual data. Rank cross-sectionally at each fiscal year-end and hold for the subsequent 12 months, skipping 4 months to ensure data availability.", "rationale": "Inventory building that outpaces sales signals softening demand and future markdowns, so firms overaccumulating inventory relative to throughput subsequently disappoint.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than COGS)"},
{"name": "Accrual-to-Cashflow Reliability Ratio", "construction": "Compute total accruals as (change in current assets minus change in cash) minus (change in current liabilities minus change in short-term debt) minus depreciation, all from the annual balance sheet and income statement (Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, DP). Scale by absolute operating cash flow proxied by net income plus depreciation. Rank each June and hold 12 months.", "rationale": "Earnings driven heavily by accruals rather than cash are less persistent and tend to be overvalued, so high-accrual firms underperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (cash-backed earnings)"},
{"name": "Dividend Initiation Momentum", "construction": "Flag firms whose most recent quarterly dividend per share (CRSP distribution files) exceeds zero when the same quarter one year earlier paid zero. Form a long portfolio of newly initiating firms and hold for 12 months, rebalancing monthly.", "rationale": "Dividend initiations credibly signal management's confidence in sustainable future cash flows and reduce free-cash-flow agency costs, leading to positive drift.", "higher_returns_for": "firms that recently initiated dividends"},
{"name": "Asset Turnover Improvement", "construction": "Compute asset turnover as sales (SALE) divided by average total assets (AT) for the current and prior fiscal year; take the year-over-year change. Rank cross-sectionally each June, hold 12 months.", "rationale": "Rising asset turnover reflects improving operational efficiency and capacity utilization that the market underappreciates, forecasting higher profitability and returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (improving turnover)"},
{"name": "Capital Expenditure Restraint", "construction": "Compute capital expenditures (CAPX) scaled by lagged total assets (AT), then subtract the firm's own trailing three-year average of the same ratio. Rank each June and hold 12 months.", "rationale": "Firms sharply increasing investment above their historical norm tend to overinvest and destroy value, while restraint relative to history preserves returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (below-normal capex)"},
{"name": "Gross Margin Stability", "construction": "Compute gross margin ((SALE - COGS)/SALE) for each of the past five fiscal years and take its standard deviation. Rank cross-sectionally each June, hold 12 months.", "rationale": "Stable gross margins indicate durable pricing power and lower fundamental risk that is nevertheless mispriced given investor preference for growth volatility.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (stable margins)"},
{"name": "Short-Term Debt Reliance Shift", "construction": "Compute the ratio of short-term debt (DLC) to total debt (DLC + DLTT) at fiscal year-end and take the year-over-year change. Rank each June and hold 12 months.", "rationale": "A rising reliance on short-term financing signals rollover and refinancing risk plus possible constrained access to long-term capital, predicting lower returns due to distress.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (declining short-term debt reliance)"},
{"name": "Sales-Weighted Price Reversal", "construction": "Interact the prior-month return (CRSP) with the log of trailing-twelve-month sales (SALE) percentile: form the standard short-term reversal signal (negative prior-month return) but restrict the effect to large-sales firms by using prior-month return multiplied by an indicator for above-median sales. Rank monthly, hold one month.", "rationale": "Short-term reversal from liquidity provision is stronger among high-sales established firms where price moves are less informative and more likely temporary.", "higher_returns_for": "large-sales firms with low (most negative) prior-month returns"},
{"name": "Retained Earnings Intensity", "construction": "Compute cumulative retained earnings (RE) scaled by total assets (AT) at fiscal year-end. Rank cross-sectionally each June and hold 12 months.", "rationale": "High retained-earnings intensity reflects a firm's accumulated internally-financed profitability and maturity, associated with lower risk of external financing distress and steady returns.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure"},
{"name": "Selling Expense Efficiency Trend", "construction": "Compute selling, general and administrative expense (XSGA) divided by sales (SALE) and take the year-over-year change. Rank cross-sectionally each June and hold 12 months.", "rationale": "A falling SG&A-to-sales ratio signals improving operating leverage and cost discipline that predicts future earnings surprises and higher returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (declining SG&A ratio)"}]}
